summary_of_reasoning: Zero candidates. Traced every path by which a before-hash reaches a verifier, and every path by which an inner (uarch) result settles an enclosing match, in the released Dave contracts (Tournament.sol, Match.sol, Commitment.sol, MatchClocks.sol, Clock.sol, MultiLevelTournamentFactory.sol, CartesiStateTransition.sol, ArbitrationConstants.sol, DaveConsensus.sol) and in the referee model of doc/recipes/prt.lua (validate_claim_response, validate_bisection_response, advance_bisection, validate_seal_response, open_uarch_tournament, propagate_uarch_result, settle_divergence, settle_uarch_state_hash, validate_state_transition_response). (1) Before-hash. Dave Match.sealDivergence -> _requireAgreeState: at divergencePosition 0 it requires agreeState == args.initialHash. For the root tournament that is DaveConsensus's initialMachineStateHash or the staged and accepted finalMachineStateHash. For an inner tournament it is the parent's verified agreeState. Otherwise it authenticates agreeState as leaf divergencePosition-1 against the revealing commitment, with a sibling count equal to the height. The bisection invariant (each commitment's frontier node is hash-chained to its root, and descending right happens only when both left children are equal) makes that leaf common to both claims. winLeafMatch passes exactly divergence.agreeState, and instantiateInner passes the same _agreeHash that _requireAgreeState checked. The Lua model mirrors this: it checks the proof address, the size, the sibling count, the root of the turn claim and, when descending right, target_hash == turn_left_node. At leaf 0 it uses tournament.initial_state_hash, which for a uarch tournament is the mcycle agreed state. cartesi.keccak256 rejects inputs that are not 32 bytes long, so a length trick cannot pass a subtree root off as a leaf. (2) Reveal parity. Commitment one reveals first, so the revealer at height 1 is commitment one iff the height is odd. Heights 54 and 38 are both even, so the revealer is commitment two, and the code maps finalStateOne and finalStateTwo correctly. (3) Uarch-claim admission. joinTournament -> requireValidContestedFinalState requires the authenticated last leaf (getRootForLastLeaf) to equal one of nestedDispute.contestedFinalStateOne or contestedFinalStateTwo. The Lua model checks final == next_state_hashes[1] or [2] after a last-leaf proof at full height. The contested states always differ: the parents differ at every level by induction, and claims with equal roots are merged, or barred by Clock.requireUninitialized. (4) Inner result. Tournament.innerResult maps finalStates[candidate] to the parent commitment through _parentCommitment(nestedDispute). winInnerTournament consumes only children recorded in matchIdFromInnerTournaments by its own seal; orphan clones from the permissionless factory are ignored. The Lua propagate_uarch_result and settle_divergence compare winner.final_state_hash with next_state_hashes. Neither depends on who posted the claim. A sealed inner match keeps both clocks paused with a positive allowance (Clock._pausedState asserts it), so winMatchByTimeout and eliminateMatchByTimeout classify NONE and cannot bypass the child. (5) Constants. The meta-cycle is 24+48+20 = 92 bits. Level 0 has log2step 38 and height 54, so 38+54 = 92. Level 1 has log2step 0 and height 38, matching the level-0 stride. So the last leaf of the inner tree is the transition at counter (p<<38)+2^38-1, whose low 20 bits are all ones (step+reset). That leaf is the parent's leaf p, and toCycle(p) indexes the transition out of the agree state.
not_covered: Clock arithmetic and timeout windows: winner-expiry elimination of both parent claims (INNER_ELIMINABLE_WINNER_EXPIRED), the leaf-race earlier-deadline rule, and refill/envelope sizing. These belong to A7, not A1, and were read only as far as they bear on whether a sealed inner match can be decided without its child.
machine-solidity-step internals (UArchStep, UArchReset, SendCmioResponse, AccessLogs): whether they bind the log to machineState correctly. I did not check them; that is R3/R10.

Whether the honest operator's computation-hash builders put the same canonical hashes at the leaf positions Dave assumes (mcycle-boundary, rejection-exception and fixed-point leaves). That is R2/R4/R6; A1 was checked only structurally, given correct leaves.
DaveConsensus input bounds and provideMerkleRootOfInput (A3), and output and machine-validity proofs (A5).
The Lua transport and schema decoding (game-transport.lua): whether malformed responses can crash or stall the referee model (A8).
The Lua PRT bridge (prt-bridge.lua) and players, which are support components; their A1 handling of NewInnerTournament events and agree-state proofs was only skimmed.
No experiments were run; the conclusions rest on code reading only.
